reachable: Not applicable in the scored-position sense, and correctly so. This is a training-time sampler: make_batcher returns next_batch(step, total_steps) -> list[int], and harness._train (line 78-83) uses that list only to index fit_stripped before stream.collate builds the tensors. load_batcher is referenced in exactly two places repo-wide (evolve/harness.py:78, eval/smoke.py:17) and nowhere in cups_probe.py / cdh_probe.py / cups_ca.py / eval/adapter.py's scoring path, so the batcher is never called at scoring time. Nothing in the impl touches key_pad, observations, exit codes or targets — _deepest_routed_read takes only s["cmds"], and the only other field read is s.get("image"). There is therefore no branch that could switch behaviour at the scored read, where the observation is withheld. The mechanism gets "gradient" in the only sense available to a batcher: every selected row participates in the listwise loss each step, and the composition change is live from step 1 (ramps at depth_ramp_frac=0.35 and ramp_frac=0.3 of the budget). Cost is negligible: 0.04s setup + 1.45s for 4000 batches on a 4000-sequence corpus.
solves_outside_model: No leak, but it deserves an explicit statement because the shape is superficially the retracted one. _deepest_routed_read DOES resolve the move/redirection chain in Python and recover the ground-truth origin path of the content the read returns — I confirmed the resolution is genuinely correct, because the derived CROSSED flag reproduces the generator's own routed_idx != name_idx on 21/21 sequences where the cups read is the deepest read. That resolved answer is then reduced to three per-sequence scalars (hop count, suffix-stripped address string, boolean) which are consumed only to bias index selection. The function returns a Python list of ints; no tensor, no token, no loss term, no head input depends on the parse, and the same sequence produces byte-identical tokens regardless of which batch it lands in, so batch membership cannot carry information into the model's input. This is the permitted case (parsing commands to choose SAMPLES). It is also structurally outside the stream axis's read-token-parity invariant, but that invariant is not needed here: a sampler has no channel to the read token at all. Verified no mutation of the sequences handed in (deepcopy comparison after 5 batches on two corpora).
summary:
The code is a faithful implementation of its own MECHANICAL description and is structurally safe. Every mechanical claim I could execute checks out: the backward chain-walk equals the recorded cups depth on 23/24 jail sequences with the single disagreement being exactly the cvar redirection chain the author describes (row 5, /tmp/w/cvar/g1/c1.dat, parsed 2 vs recorded 1); the deep/shallow stratum assignment is 24/24 correct; the CROSSED flag matches the generator's routed_idx != name_idx 21/21; the "max chain 6 vs supervised depth 2" example reproduces exactly (row 14). The sampler returns exactly bs indices, in bounds, deterministic given the seed and seed-sensitive, mutates nothing, and survives every degenerate corpus (1 sequence, 1 image, no moves, empty/absent/None cmds, missing image key) at bs in {1,7,64}. The genome differs from parent r4-01-routing-depth-systematic on the batcher axis only, verified against evolve/archive/genomes.jsonl. The impl installed in evolve/chunks/batcher/ is byte-identical to the proposal file. No INTEGRATION_FIX.md exists.

What diverges is the RATIONALE, and it is the load-bearing part. The hypothesis argues the candidate should work because the baseline batch essentially never contains two rows that share a read address and disagree about the answer, so "the command at a routed-read row is very nearly a unique key for its target". That is measurably false on the very file the author says they checked. There are only 9 core address families in the entire generator vocabulary, the move-index suffix runs 1..8, and 63% of supervised reads land on a core family — so a uniform 64-sequence batch already contains ~11 exact-read-command collisions with different answers and ~89 family collisions, essentially with certainty. Four of the 24 sampled sequences already share an exact read command with a different answer. The candidate raises collision density roughly 2x and concentrates it on 3 keys; that is a real change, but it is a change of degree over an already-collided baseline, not the removal of an absent constraint. The second claimed mechanism (crossed/aligned balancing) shifts a corpus rate of 0.583 to 0.5 and is close to a no-op. The corrected depth parse is a genuine improvement over the parent but a 2-in-24 one on the quantity that is actually consumed.

Net: this is a legitimate, well-built, cheap sampler change that should be scored — but the description it would be archived under attributes its expected effect to a property of the data that does not hold, which will mislead whoever breeds from it.

divergences.claim: "the objective's in-batch negatives almost never contain two rows that share a read address and disagree about the answer" / "In a uniform or image-blocked batch, the command at a routed-read row is very nearly a unique key for its target, so minimising the listwise contrastive loss does not require the trajectory at all." This is the entire WHY-THIS-SHOULD-MOVE-THE-MEASURED-QUANTITY argument.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code does raise collision density, but it is removing a constraint that is already abundantly present, not one that is absent. Measured on the jail sample: across all 24 boards there are only 9 distinct core address families (/tmp/w/cups/{etc/ssh/sshd_config.cfg, usr/local/etc/app.ini, usr/share/misc/magic.txt, etc/cron.d/backup.job, etc/nginx/nginx.conf, opt/app/conf/settings.yaml, var/lib/misc/state.db, var/log/syslog.log, var/spool/mail/root.msg}), the move-index suffix ranges over 1..8, and 15/24 (63%) of supervised reads land on a core family. In a random draw of only 24 sequences, 4 already share an EXACT read command string with a different answer (`cat /tmp/w/cups/usr/local/etc/app.ini.6` x3 with 3 distinct outputs; `magic.txt.1` x2; `sshd_config.cfg.7` x2). Simulating the baseline_uniform batcher at bs=64 against that vocabulary gives ~11 exact-read-command colliding pairs and ~89 family-colliding pairs per batch, with P(no exact collision) = 0.0000. On a resampled 800-sequence corpus, baseline_uniform gave 119 exact-cmd colliding pairs/batch vs the candidate's 257 — a ~2x increase, not a categorical change.
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/rev-slot22/collide.py (baseline_uniform 119.0 exact-cmd pairs, 209.8 family pairs, 33.7 deep rows per batch; candidate 256.7 / 367.3 / 51.7). Vocabulary + exact-duplicate counts derived directly from evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl meta.cups.final_loc and the cups_test cmd strings. Birthday simulation of a uniform 64-batch: 11.1 exact-cmd colliding pairs, 89.1 family colliding pairs, P(zero)=0.0000.

divergences.claim: "Origin-family balance inside a block... A key's slots are split between its crossed and its aligned members at cross_frac, so inside a block the read address carries no information about whether the answer is the content that originally lived under that name." Presented as removing "the second zero-scoring strategy the same way" as the collision block.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code does implement the split (draw(addr_cross[j], m_c) / draw(addr_align[j], m - m_c) when m>=2 and both sub-pools are non-empty), but the corpus is already near-balanced: the crossed rate (routed_idx != name_idx) among depth>=3 reads in the jail sample is 0.583 (7 crossed / 5 aligned), and 0.625 overall. cross_frac=0.5 therefore shifts the in-block composition by ~8 percentage points. The claimed mechanism is real but its measured effect size is near a no-op, not comparable in force to the collision block.
divergences.evidence: Counter over evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl meta.cups: {(crossed=True, deep=True): 7, (False, True): 5, (True, False): 8, (False, False): 4}; crossed rate deep = 0.5833.

divergences.claim: "The parent's max-over-board number and that depth disagree badly on real sequences (one sample: max chain 6, depth of the supervised read 2), because the deepest chain in a trajectory usually belongs to a content that is never read."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The cited example is exact and reproduces (sequence index 14: recorded cups depth 2, parent's _routing_depth 6, child's parse 2). But 'disagree badly' and 'usually' overstate it: the parent's max-over-board equals the recorded cups depth on 20/24, and — what actually matters, since deep_min only ever induces a two-way stratum split — the parent agrees with ground truth on the depth>=3 boundary on 22/24. The child is better (23/24 exact, 24/24 on the stratum boundary), but the improvement over the parent is 2 sequences in 24 on the quantity the batcher consumes, not a wholesale correction.
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/rev-slot22/parent_cmp.py: gt==parent 20/24, gt==child 23/24, stratum agreement parent 22/24, child 24/24, worst parent overshoot (gt=2, parent=6).

divergences.claim: "A ramped `addr_share` of the batch is filled from a few of those keys." (hypothesis section 2)
divergences.what_the_code_does: addr_share is a share of the BLOCK, not of the batch: n_block = round(bs * block_frac_max * r); n_addr = round(n_block * share). At full ramp with the genome's params (bs=64 default from optim, block_frac_max=0.75, addr_share=0.6) that is 29/64 = 45% of the batch, not 60%. The chunk DESCRIPTION states it correctly ("a ramped share of the batch"); only the hypothesis wording is off.
divergences.evidence: lines 173-176 of the impl; bs defaults to 64 because genome.json's optim chunk carries no "bs" key (evolve/genome.py:26).

divergences.claim: "Exact duplicate rows are harmless here (the objective's ring gives near-identical targets ~0 negative weight) but they consume slots."
divergences.what_the_code_does: r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives zeroes only the BOOST for near-identical targets (dupmask = 1 - exp(-tt/DELTA) -> 0, so a_raw -> 1), then row-normalizes a by the row mean; a duplicate keeps a non-zero, roughly 1/row_mean weight in the softmax denominator, and an exact-duplicate sequence (identical pred and identical target, dist2 = 0 off-diagonal) contributes an irreducible loss floor at every one of its ~30 command rows. Measured duplication: 2-5 of 64 slots per batch on a corpus whose address pools were 20 deep. Small in the intended regime, but 'harmless / ~0 negative weight' is not what the objective does.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/objective/r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives.py lines 60-67 (a_raw = 1 + KAPPA*ring; a = a_raw / row_mean, masked_fill(eye, 1.0)); uniq-index counts 56-62/64 from /private/tmp/rev-slot22/run_batcher.py on the 480-sequence corpus.

divergences.claim: Failure mode as stated: "If the training split's routed reads land on mostly unique addresses... the collision tier is empty and the candidate degrades to the partner's image blocking plus a corrected depth stratification — a small change, likely inside the noise."
divergences.what_the_code_does: In the addr-empty regime the degradation is not neutral. share is forced to 0, so all 48 block slots become image-block slots that are only power-tilted on depth, and the two-stratum deep allocation governs only the 16 free slots. On the 24-sequence jail corpus (where no family reaches min_block=4, so have_addr is False) the deep share of the whole batch at step 4000 fell to 12/64 = 19% against a 50% corpus deep rate — i.e. the fallback can actively REDUCE deep supervision below the baseline, rather than being 'a small change'. The evidence says this regime is unlikely on the real split, but the hypothesis under-describes it.
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/rev-slot22/run_batcher.py, 24-seq corpus: deep(>=3) rows per 64 = 32, 35, 42, 53, 12 at steps 1/200/600/1200/4000; corpus deep rate is 12/24 = 50%. Address families among deep reads in that corpus max out at 3 members, below min_block=4.
